problem:
Consider the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ is the unique solution to the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.
$$

A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x(0)$ is presented below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$  

$\text{L2}:\,$ $x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c$ for some constant vector $c$  

$\text{L3}:\,$ $x(0)={Φ}_{0}(0)\,c$  

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $x(0)=c$  

$\text{L6}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}\,x(0)$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ follows from $\text{L2}$ by {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines $\text{L3}$ and $\text{L4}$ by  {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line $\text{L2}$ by substitution from lines {{field-3}}.

feedback.problem:
Consider the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. You're given that the standard fundamental matrix ${Φ}_{0}(t)$ is the unique solution to the initial value problem

$$
{Φ}_{0}^{′}(t)=A{Φ}_{0}(t),\,{Φ}_{0}(0)={I}_{n}.
$$

A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x({t}_{0})$ is presented below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$

$\text{L2}:\,$ $x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c$ for some constant vector $c$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}\,c$ 

$\text{L4}:\,$ $x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}x({t}_{0})=({e}^{A{t}_{0}})^{-1}{e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c$

$\text{L6}:\,$ $c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At}{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L8}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{At-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\,$

$\text{L9}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})\,$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L2}$ is true by {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from $\text{L3}$ {{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ follows from $\text{L7}$ by the fact that {{field-3}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}.$ Since ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is a fundamental matrix for the system, every solution of the system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c\,\text{for some constant vector }c.
$$

Thus, $\text{L2}$ is true by $\text{the properties of a fundamental matrix}.$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$ and $\text{L4}.$ Starting from $\text{L3},$

$$
x(t)={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

we evaluate both sides at $t={t}_{0}$ to obtain

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c
$$

which is line $\text{L4}.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from $\text{L3}$ $\text{by substituting }t={t}_{0}.$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L7}$ and $\text{L8}.$ Since $At$ and $-A{t}_{0}$ commute, we can use the property 

$$
{e}^{At}{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}={e}^{At-A{t}_{0}}.
$$

Substituting this into line $\text{L7},$ we get line $\text{L8}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{At-A{t}_{0}}x({t}_{0})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ follows from $\text{L7}$ by the fact that ${e}^{X}{e}^{Y}={e}^{X+Y}\text{ when }X\text{ and }Y\text{ commute}.$
